The resolved date binds as an ordinary `loParam`/`hiParam` value (never interpolated, DVT-7). Sub-day units (`hour`, `minute`) bind resolved absolute timestamps (ISO 8601 datetime, not a calendar date). Used inside `relativeDate.lo`/`relativeDate.hi`; an omitted end is open-ended.

unit.description: Calendar unit of the offset. Sub-day units (`hour`, `minute`) resolve to an absolute timestamp bound; day and coarser units resolve to a calendar date bound.

amount.description: Non-negative count of `unit`s offset from the anchor. `0` = the anchor itself ('today' / period start as the resolver defines).

direction.description: Whether the offset is before (`past`) or after (`future`) the anchor.

FilterSpec.description: Spec for a filter control element (DVT-140, ADR-0028): a dashboard-level, query-bound control whose selected value re-queries its target panels. dvt Core (renderer-neutral). The filter's selectable options come from the panel's own `data` (an author-written `SELECT DISTINCT`-style value-source query, or baked `data.rows`), or from a static `values` list. The selected value binds into target panels' SQL by NAME — target panels declare a matching named placeholder `%(param)s` and a `data.params` entry; the value overwrites that entry only (never interpolated, never reorders — ADR-0028). Scalar controls bind a single value; the `multiselect` control binds an ARRAY of values that the engine expands into a parameter-bound IN-list per driver (DVT-170) — the target panel writes a bare named placeholder, e.g. `WHERE region IN %(region)s`. A RANGE filter (operator `between`, or control `number-range`/`date-range` — DVT-257/256) binds TWO author-declared scalar keys (`loParam`/`hiParam`) instead of a single `param`: the author writes `WHERE (col >= %(lo)s OR %(lo)s IS NULL) AND (col <= %(hi)s OR %(hi)s IS NULL)` and a `data.params` entry per bound (ADR-0028 Amendment 1 A2.2/A3/A4.2); each bound overwrites independently and an unset side binds typed NULL (open-ended). For a range, the scalar `param` is FORBIDDEN and `loParam`+`hiParam` are REQUIRED (A7).

param.description: The params key this filter sets on its target panels (scalar/single-select/multiselect/text). A target panel must declare a matching named placeholder `%(param)s` in its query and a `data.params` entry with this key; the filter overwrites that value only. REQUIRED for non-range filters; FORBIDDEN for a range filter (operator `between` or control `number-range`/`date-range`), which uses `loParam`/`hiParam` instead (ADR-0028 Amendment 1 A7).

loParam.description: Lower-bound params key for a RANGE filter (operator `between`, or control `number-range`/`date-range` — ADR-0028 Amendment 1 A2.2/A3). An ordinary author-declared `data.params` key (no synthetic `__lo` suffix) — the author writes the predicate (e.g. `WHERE (amount >= %(amount_lo)s OR %(amount_lo)s IS NULL) AND …`) and the FilterSpec points at it here. REQUIRED with `hiParam` when the filter is a range (and `param` then forbidden). An unset lower bound binds typed NULL (open-ended; A4.2). Zero engine change — it is a normal named bind.

hiParam.description: Upper-bound params key for a RANGE filter (ADR-0028 Amendment 1 A2.2/A3). An ordinary author-declared `data.params` key (no synthetic `__hi` suffix). REQUIRED with `loParam` when the filter is a range. An unset upper bound binds typed NULL (open-ended; A4.2).

min.description: Number-range slider lower bound (the leftmost slider value). Optional; when omitted the renderer derives the slider domain from the value-source result (a `MIN()`/`MAX()` light query over the bound column, row-capped + RBAC-scoped per ADR-0011) and otherwise falls back to the data extent. Slider chrome only — never enters SQL (the bound VALUE does). dvt Core (DVT-257).

max.description: Number-range slider upper bound (the rightmost slider value). Optional; see `min` for domain derivation. Slider chrome only — never enters SQL. dvt Core (DVT-257).

step.description: Number-range slider/arrow-key increment. Optional; defaults to 1. Slider chrome only — never enters SQL. dvt Core (DVT-257).

valueField.description: Column of the value-source result (data.rows / value query) holding each option's bound value.

labelField.description: Optional column holding each option's display label. Defaults to valueField.

control.description: Control kind. Default select. `multiselect` binds an array of selected values to the named param; the engine expands the array into a parameter-bound IN-list per driver (DVT-170, never interpolated). The target panel uses a bare named placeholder, e.g. `WHERE region IN %(region)s`. An empty multiselect selection matches no rows. `toggle` renders a tri-state switch (true / false / unset) and binds a single scalar boolean via the `equals` operator path; use with `valueType:'boolean'`. Unset = no predicate when `unsetMode:'omit'` (default), or SQL NULL when `unsetMode:'null'`. `number` renders a single numeric `<input type=number>` that binds one scalar value to `param` — use with `operator: gt | gte | lt | lte | equals` for one-sided numeric comparisons (DVT-538). Unlike `number-range` it binds a single `param` key, not `loParam`/`hiParam`. `segmented` and `button-group` are alternate INLINE renderings of single-select (same value binding as `select`) — a horizontal row of option buttons where exactly one is active; ideal for ≤6 options. `radio` is an alternate inline rendering of single-select — a vertical radio list; same value binding as `select`. `checkbox-list` is an alternate inline rendering of multiselect (same array binding as `multiselect`, engine expands to IN-list, DVT-170) — an inline vertical checkbox list without a popover. All four inline controls commit instantly (no Apply step) and reuse the same option source (spec.values or value-source query rows) as their popover counterparts. `top-n` ranks the value-source query rows by a measure column (`measureField`), keeps the top or bottom N options, and binds the resulting set as a parameter-bound IN-list (same binding as `multiselect`). The viewer can adjust N with a compact stepper; the author sets the initial N (`n`, default 10) and ranking direction (`order`: `desc` = Top-N, `asc` = Bottom-N). Client-side only — no engine rewrite. DVT-541.

measureField.description: Column in the value-source query result holding the numeric measure used to rank options for a `top-n` control (DVT-541). The control sorts rows by this column (descending for Top-N, ascending for Bottom-N per `order`), keeps the top `n` options, and binds the resulting values as a parameter-bound IN-list. Ignored for all other control kinds.

n.description: How many top or bottom options the `top-n` control keeps and binds as an IN-list (DVT-541). Default 10. The viewer can adjust this at view time with the control's compact stepper. Ignored for all other control kinds.

order.description: Ranking direction for the `top-n` control (DVT-541). `desc` (default) = keep the N options with the HIGHEST measure values (Top-N). `asc` = keep the N options with the LOWEST measure values (Bottom-N). Ignored for all other control kinds.

valueType.description: Type the selected value is coerced to before binding (defense-in-depth; binding is the security boundary). Default string.

targets.description: Which panels re-query on selection. "all" (default) = every panel on the page that declares the param key; an explicit list of panel ids; or the structured scope form (ADR-0028 Amendment 4 C1). A panel that doesn't declare the param key is never re-fetched regardless. The shorthands "all" and [panelId,...] expand to {scope:"page", panels:<that>}.

scope.description: Which pages the filter applies to. "page" (default) = only the page the filter element lives on (current behavior). "pages" = an explicit allow-list (pages[] required). "dashboard" = every page (report-level). ADR-0028 Amendment 4 C2.

pages.description: Page ids the filter applies to. Required iff scope=="pages"; ignored otherwise.

panels.description: Panels within the resolved page set that re-query. "all" (default) = every declaring panel; or an explicit panel-id list.

bindings.description: Per-target column remapping and per-panel mode override (ADR-0028 Amendment 4 C4). Each entry overrides — never widens — targeting for a panel already in the resolved target set: it redirects the filter value into a differently-named authored params key (`as`) and/or overrides the interaction mode (`mode`) for that panel only.

panel.description: Panel id already in the resolved target set whose binding is overridden.

as.description: The authored data.params key on the target panel that receives the value (must be a key the panel already declares; otherwise a no-op + lint warning).

mode.description: Per-target interaction mode override (ADR-0028 Amendment 4 C4). Overrides the top-level targets.mode for this panel only. Precedence: bindings[panel].mode > targets.mode > "filter".

How a targeted panel reacts (ADR-0028 Amendment 4 C3). "filter" (default) = re-query the warehouse. "highlight" = client-side dim of non-matching marks on already-fetched rows, NO re-query (ADR-0011 safe). "none" = explicit opt-out (suppress reaction).

oneOf.description: Structured scope form (ADR-0028 Amendment 4 C1). Back-compat shorthands "all" and [panelId,...] expand to {scope:"page", panels:<that>}.

values.description: Static option list — the fallback when there is no value-source query/rows. Each item is a scalar value, or an object { value, label }.

default.description: Authored default selection (versioned spec state, ADR-0021). Omit / null = unset (no value bound; target panels use their authored param default). A `multiselect` control may default to an array of values.

label.description: Display label for the filter control (shown in the pill header / popover chrome). Falls back to `placeholder`, then the param name, then 'Filter'. Use this instead of overloading `placeholder`, which reverts to true input-placeholder semantics (hint text inside a text input). dvt Core.

placeholder.description: Placeholder text shown inside a text/search input when empty. To label the control, use `label` instead.

help.description: Optional help / description text for the filter control. When present, the renderer surfaces an accessible help affordance (a '?' icon) next to the control label; the text is revealed on hover and keyboard focus via aria-describedby so screen-reader and keyboard users receive it. Use for brief contextual guidance — e.g. 'Limited to active regions' or 'Date the record was last modified'. dvt Core.

allLabel.description: Display text for the unfiltered / "everything" state (ADR-0028 Amendment 1 A6) — e.g. "All regions", "Any date". The single-select "All" row and the multi-select 0-selected state are CONTROL affordances rendered by dvt, NOT authored data rows (this retires the hand-rolled 'ALL' option/sentinel pattern, DVT-254). Falls back to `placeholder`, then "All". dvt Core.

unsetMode.description: How an UNSET filter binds (ADR-0028 Amendment 1 A6). dvt Core. 'omit' (default): the key is not set in the interaction map, so each target panel keeps its AUTHORED `params` default (author writes plain `WHERE col = %(k)s`). 'null': the key binds SQL NULL (author writes the guarded `WHERE (col = %(k)s OR %(k)s IS NULL)`; required for open-ended range sides, A4.2). Unset is omit or typed NULL only — never a sentinel string or client-built SQL.

operator.description: Comparison operator (ADR-0028 Amendment 1 A1/A4). dvt Core. Default 'equals'. AUTHOR-FIXED spec state (versioned, ADR-0021) — NOT a control a viewer picks; a viewer only changes the bound VALUE. The operator governs how the runtime SHAPES the bound value before it sets `params[key]`; it never selects or constructs SQL. The AUTHOR writes the matching, immutable predicate text: equals `col = %(k)s`; not-equals `col <> %(k)s`; contains/starts-with/ends-with `col LIKE %(k)s ESCAPE '!'` (the runtime escapes `! % _` in the value with `!`, then wraps `%v%` / `v%` / `%v`); in `col IN %(k)s` / not-in `col NOT IN %(k)s` (array IN-list, DVT-170/261); between `col BETWEEN %(lo)s AND %(hi)s` (two keys, DVT-257); gt `col > %(k)s`; gte `col >= %(k)s`; lt `col < %(k)s`; lte `col <= %(k)s` (single-value numeric comparison, DVT-538 — bound as a plain scalar, no LIKE-wrap). The value enters SQL only as a bound parameter — never interpolated (DVT-7). For LIKE operators the author's query MUST carry the `ESCAPE '!'` clause.

relativeDate.description: Relative-date config for a date filter (ADR-0028 Amendment 1 A2.3/A5, DVT-256). dvt Core. Each end (`lo`/`hi`) is a relative expression `{unit, amount, direction}` that resolves to a CONCRETE absolute date before binding; an omitted/null end is OPEN-ENDED on that side. Resolution is DETERMINISTIC: 'now' is sampled ONCE per query request from the UTC clock and the author-declared `timezone` (below) drives day boundaries; the resolved absolute bounds bind as ordinary `date`/`timestamp` scalars to `loParam`/`hiParam` (the no-interpolation invariant DVT-7/ADR-0028 §1 is preserved — relative dates never enter SQL as text, never use the warehouse `CURRENT_DATE`). The client never trusts its own clock for sharing: URL state encodes the relative EXPRESSION, not the resolved dates, so a shared link re-resolves vs the viewer's current 'now'. Used only with `control:date-range`; the scalar `param` stays forbidden (a date range binds `loParam`/`hiParam`, A7).

lo.description: Lower-bound relative expression (resolves to the absolute `loParam` value). Omit for an open-ended start.

hi.description: Upper-bound relative expression (resolves to the absolute `hiParam` value). Omit for an open-ended end. `{amount:0}` = the anchor ('today').

presets.description: Allow-list of quick-preset chips offered on a date filter (ADR-0028 Amendment 1 A2.3, DVT-256). dvt Core. Each preset resolves to a relative window deterministically (server/query-time, same 'now'/timezone basis as `relativeDate`, A5) and binds the resolved absolute bounds to `loParam`/`hiParam`. Closed enum: `today`, `last-7d`, `last-30d`, `last-90d`, `mtd` (month-to-date), `qtd` (quarter-to-date), `ytd` (year-to-date), `all-time` (clears both bounds). An unrecognized token fails validation closed.

timezone.description: IANA timezone name (e.g. `America/New_York`) that defines the day-boundary basis for relative-date resolution (ADR-0028 Amendment 1 A5, DVT-256). dvt Core. Default `UTC`. Versioned author spec state — what 'today' / 'last 7 days' means is computed against THIS timezone server-side, NOT the viewer's locale, so a dashboard resolves identically for every viewer. Drives only relative-date day boundaries; the resolved bounds themselves bind as ordinary date params.

chrome.description: Card chrome override for a filter element (DVT-550). Default 'card' (omit for existing behavior): renders the filter inside the standard surface/border/shadow card with its minHeight floor. 'none': renders the bare control only — no background, no border, no box-shadow, no border-radius, and no minHeight floor. Use 'none' to embed a filter pill directly in a layout without the doubled-chrome / wasted-space of a card-in-card appearance. dvt Core.

apply.description: Author override for when the filter commits its selection to target panels (DVT-535). Omit for the default per-control behavior: instant controls (select, search, toggle, number) commit on each change; batched controls (multiselect, number-range, date-range) hold in a draft until the viewer presses the Apply button. 'button' forces an explicit Apply step even for normally-instant controls (select/search/toggle/number) — useful when a filter re-queries an expensive panel and immediate commits on every click would be jarring. 'live' forces immediate commits even for normally-batched controls (multiselect, number-range, date-range) — use when the target panels are cheap to query and the author wants zero-latency feedback. The commit TIMING is the only thing that changes; the value binding semantics (ADR-0028 §1) are identical regardless. dvt Core.

required.description: When true, no clear affordance (✕ / 'All' row) is shown and target panels do NOT query until the viewer makes an explicit selection (DVT-535). Prevents a 'fetch everything then filter' pattern on expensive panels where an unfiltered query would be too broad or nonsensical. Default false (omit for existing behavior): filters are optional and target panels always query, using the authored data.params default when the filter is unset. ADR-0028 §1 invariant preserved: the value binding is unchanged; only the timing and optionality of the commit differ. dvt Core.

width.description: Intrinsic width of the filter control within its grid cell (DVT-536). dvt Core. Default omit = 'full': the control spans its full grid-cell width (existing behavior). 'compact': the control shrinks to its content width (fit-content), so a narrow filter (e.g. a date toggle) does not stretch across a wide grid cell. Independent of the grid cell size — the cell still occupies its authored column span; only the control's OWN footprint changes. Back-compat: omitting this field is identical to 'full'.

density.description: Vertical density of the filter control (DVT-536). dvt Core. Default omit = 'comfortable': standard 36px min-height pill with 6px top / 12px bottom padding (existing behavior). 'compact': a tighter 28px min-height pill with 4px top / 8px bottom padding — use when multiple filters share a filter-bar (DVT-551) or limited vertical space. Back-compat: omitting this field is identical to 'comfortable'.

icon.description: Leading glyph shown inside the filter pill (DVT-536). dvt Core. Closed allow-set (ADR-0032 §A3 — same discipline as `typography.fontFamily`): values outside this list fail schema validation (422). No SVG/URL/free-text is accepted. Omit (default) = no leading icon. Curated set: 'calendar' = date/time filters, 'search' = text/search filters, 'filter' = general filter, 'region' = geographic scope, 'tag' = category/label filters, 'clock' = time-of-day filters, 'user' = person/owner filters, 'dollar' = currency/financial filters. The glyph is rendered as an inline SVG with no additional icon library dependency.

placement.description: Where the filter control is shown (ADR-0028 Amendment 4 C2 / DVT-552). "page" (default) = inside its page's grid (today). "report" = shown once in a persistent dashboard-level region on every page, never duplicated. Placement is orthogonal to targets.scope (where the filter APPLIES) — a report-placed filter typically pairs with targets:{scope:"dashboard"}.

showOnPages.description: For placement:"report" only — an allow-list of page ids on which to show the control. Absent = shown on every page. Ignored for placement:"page".

searchMode.description: Option-list search mode for select and multiselect controls (DVT-540, ADR-0028 Amendment 1). dvt Core. 'client' (default / omit): the search box filters the already-fetched option list in the browser — zero extra queries, works for up to thousands of options. 'server': debounced keystrokes re-run the filter's own value-source query with the typed text bound as a LIKE-escaped named parameter (searchParam); use for high-cardinality dimensions (millions of distinct values) where the full set cannot be fetched upfront. The author writes the matching predicate in the value-source query (e.g. WHERE label LIKE %(q)s ESCAPE '!'); the runtime escapes LIKE metacharacters with '!' and wraps the term (%term%) before binding — values are NEVER interpolated (ADR-0011 / ADR-0028 Amendment 1 A4). Ignored for all control kinds other than select and multiselect.

searchParam.description: Named parameter the server-side typeahead search term is bound to (DVT-540). Required when searchMode:'server'; ignored otherwise. The author's value-source query must declare a matching %(searchParam)s placeholder with data.params. The runtime LIKE-escapes the viewer's typed text with '!' and wraps it as %term% before binding — never interpolated (ADR-0011 / ADR-0028 §A4.1).

allOf.$comment: ADR-0028 Amendment 1 A7: a RANGE filter (operator `between`, or control `number-range`/`date-range`) binds two author-declared keys — `loParam`+`hiParam` are REQUIRED and the scalar `param` is FORBIDDEN (a range is not a scalar filter). Otherwise the scalar `param` is REQUIRED (base ADR-0028) and the range keys are not used. One key set = one operator family.

DVT-540: searchParam is REQUIRED when searchMode is 'server'. A server-mode filter without searchParam validates clean but silently no-ops (the runtime has no key to bind the LIKE-escaped search term to). Enforce here so authors catch the mistake at apply time rather than at query time.

ContainerSpec.description: Spec for a container element (DVT-114, ADR-0030): a layout primitive that holds several panel SETS behind tabs within one page region. dvt Core (renderer-neutral). Children stay REAL elements in the page's panels[] (ADR-0021 — never inlined); each tab references them by id and carries its own mini 24-col Layout scoped to that tab's children. The container itself occupies one cell in the page's outer layout.items by its own id; its children are NOT in the page grid (they are placed by the tab layout). Single level only: a container may not contain another container (no tabs-in-tabs). Referential integrity (refs exist, no double-placement, no nesting, defaultTab valid, per-page element ceiling) is enforced by a Go semantic pass at apply time — JSON Schema cannot express cross-element references. NOT the same as page-level tabs (pages[] + tabBar), which switch whole pages.

layout.description: Container layout mode. v1 ships "tabs"; the const leaves room for splits/accordion later.

defaultTab.description: Id of the tab active on first render. Defaults to the first tab when unset; an id that matches no tab is rejected by the semantic pass.

tabs.description: Ordered tab definitions. At least one; capped to bound fan-out (DoS-in-the-large).

id.description: Tab id (unique within the container; must not collide with any panel id on the page). Conservative charset — tab ids are wired via React keys/ARIA, never string-interpolated into a selector.

label.description: Tab label (plain text; rendered as a React text node, auto-escaped).

panels.description: Child panel ids for this tab. Each must exist in the same page's panels[]; a child appears in at most one tab and is not a top-level page grid item (the semantic pass enforces this).

layout.description: Per-tab 24-col grid over THIS tab's child ids. Lives inside the container element's spec, so re-arranging children versions the container element (ADR-0030), not the children.

FilterBarSpec.description: Spec for a filter-bar element (DVT-551): a horizontal grouping band that lays out several filter elements inside one light, theme-aware surface. dvt Core (renderer-neutral). Children are REAL elements in the page's panels[] (ADR-0021 — never inlined), referenced by id; each renders via the normal PanelContainer so data-fetch / chrome / filters / drill all work unchanged. Intended authoring pairing: each child filter sets chrome:'none' (DVT-550) to render as a bare pill so they merge visually into a unified band without doubled chrome. Referential integrity (child ids exist in the page) is not enforced by JSON Schema — the Go semantic layer handles it at apply time (same as container). The filter-bar itself occupies one cell in the page's outer layout; its children are NOT separate page-grid items.

panels.description: Ordered ids of child filter elements in the page's panels[]. Each id must reference a panel on the same page; the semantic pass enforces existence. May be empty (bar renders as a blank band).

title.description: Optional heading displayed above the filter controls inside the band.

Drill.description: Drill-down binding on a source panel (DVT-141, ADR-0028): navigates to `targetPage` with the clicked value bound, by name, into that page's panels (`%(param)s` placeholder + a matching `data.params` entry — the same value→query contract as a filter). The value is read from the ALREADY-RENDERED click datum and becomes a bound parameter VALUE, never a SQL identifier. dvt Core; carries no code. NOTE (DVT-555): the left-click trigger for bare `drill` was removed. Drill is now invoked via a right-click context-menu drill action (`contextMenu.actions[]` with `type:"drill"`). The bare `drill` property is retained for back-compat but is inert on its own — use a `contextMenu` with a `drill` action to wire navigation, or `openOverlay` for overlay presentation. As of DVT-2719 an explicit left-click path is declarable again: `onClick` with a `drill` action. Unlike the removed DVT-555 behaviour it is never implicit — the visible affordance is mandatory and ships with the renderer in DVT-2721; until that lands a declared `onClick` validates but does not fire.

targetPage.description: Page id (pages[].id) to navigate to on click.

param.description: Params key set on the target page's panels (which must declare a matching named placeholder %(param)s).

valueFrom.description: Which part of the click supplies the bound value: 'category' (default), 'value', 'seriesName', or a field name read from the clicked row. For tables, use a field name.

valueType.description: Type the clicked value is coerced to before binding. Default string.

Brush.description: Brush-select → cross-filter binding on a source chart panel (DVT-417, ADR-0028 Amendment 2): the viewer drags a region on this chart and the brushed [lo, hi] range binds, by name, into the loParam/hiParam keys on same-page target panels (which must declare matching %(loParam)s / %(hiParam)s placeholders + data.params entries) — the same value→query contract as a range filter (Amendment 1 A3). The brushed range is read from the ALREADY-RENDERED axis and becomes two bound parameter VALUES, never SQL. dvt Core; interactive-only (a no-op in a static render); carries no code.

mode.description: Which axis the brushed range reads (1D): 'x' = horizontal range, 'y' = vertical. 2D 'rect' brush is deferred (Amendment 2 B7).

loParam.description: Authored params key bound to the range LOWER bound (Amendment 1 A3). A target panel must declare a matching %(loParam)s placeholder + data.params entry.

hiParam.description: Authored params key bound to the range UPPER bound.

valueType.description: Type the two bounds coerce to before binding. Default 'number'. A 'date' (time) axis binds ISO-string bounds.

targets.description: Which panels re-query on selection. "all" (default) = every panel on the page that declares the param key; or an explicit list of panel ids. A panel that doesn't declare the param key is never re-fetched regardless.

ContextMenu.description: Right-click context menu (ADR-0035): an ordered list of declarative actions attached to a panel's marks/rows (or a table column's cells). The viewer right-clicks a datum and the actions fire with that datum's values bound in. Carries no code — every action is declarative data (an enum `type` plus value-bearing fields). dvt Core (renderer-neutral), interactive-only (a no-op in a static render, like filter/drill). A column-level menu merges BELOW the panel-level menu (panel actions first, then column actions).

actions.description: The menu items, in display order.

ContextAction.description: One item in a right-click context menu (ADR-0035). A closed object discriminated by `type`. The clicked datum's values are available as `{token}` templates in `label` (and, for link, `url`): `{category}`, `{value}`, `{seriesName}`, and `{<field>}` for any field of the clicked row. Carries no code or $dvtRef callback.

ElementClickAction.description: A single action bound to a plain LEFT-click on a panel's datum (DVT-2719). Same vocabulary as a contextMenu action, narrowed to the navigation-safe subset: filter | drill | openOverlay. `link` was excluded by ADR-0035 Amendment 1 (deferred — DVT-2946); `copy` and `export` are deliberately excluded — they are side-effecting clipboard/download operations that must stay behind a deliberate right-click menu choice, not fire on a stray click. The action's REQUIRED `label` becomes the visible affordance text the renderer shows on hover (DVT-2721): an element that declares `onClick` is designed to always disclose that it is clickable, and that disclosure is not disableable by design. This is the point of the epic — DVT-555 removed the old implicit left-click drill precisely because it had no disclosure, so an affordance opt-out is deliberately not offered. `ContextActionWhen` and `ActionBinding` compose here unchanged, except that because `ContextActionWhen` is a per-datum guard, a `when` here makes clickability itself per-datum rather than a panel-wide toggle — only datums satisfying the guard are clickable and disclose the affordance, datums failing it are simply not clickable and show no affordance — so `when` narrows WHICH datums are clickable and is never an affordance opt-out on a datum that IS clickable. Column-level click actions on table columns are deliberately NOT part of this def (a separate, still-unshipped surface — not to be confused with the panel-level `onClick` this def IS). `onClick` is deliberately not offered on panel types that surface no CLICKED datum — no per-datum click event carrying {category}/{value}/{seriesName} bindings (`filter`, `filter-bar`, `container`, `divider`, `section`, `text`, `html`, `hero`, `media`). That is not the same as carrying no data: `text`/`html`/`hero` interpolate `{{ field | agg | format }}` against data rows and `Panel.data` is ungated on every type — see Panel's closing `allOf` constraint for the full ground. dvt Core; interactive-only — a no-op in a static render (ADR-0014 / ADR-0024 §3). Renderer coverage is full as of DVT-2722 with one exclusion: `chart:*` (including animated charts, i.e. those with an object `spec.animation`, EXCEPT `chart:line:racing` — its click carries a synthetic value-axis position as `category`, not a real category label, so it renders no affordance and dispatches nothing; DVT-3041 tracks an author-time lint advisory for this shape), `table` (mouse per data cell; the datum bound is the whole ROW — keyboard focus, `when` narrowing, and dispatch are per data row, one tab stop per actionable row), `kpi`, `stat`, and `metric-strip` (per tile) all execute the declared action with a visible affordance when it validates — cursor + hover emphasis/label for `chart:*` (mirroring the mark that was clicked), a DOM cursor/hover/focus-visible affordance plus keyboard (Enter/Space) activation for `table`/`kpi`/`stat`/`metric-strip`. What counts as actionable differs by WHAT a real click on that surface actually carries: a `chart:*` mark's click carries `category`/`value`/`seriesName` and, for a non-animated chart, a row — but only on families whose compiled series data is numeric AND row-indexed. Elsewhere a row-field binding is unreliable (DVT-3040) — the cases below illustrate that rule, they are not a closed list: on object-item families (pie/funnel/map/sunburst/treemap/sankey/gauge), on array-tuple families (scatter/heatmap/calendar), and on any family whose datum compiles to the ECharts per-datum object form — `chart:waterfall`, or any row-indexed family carrying `colorRules`, where a matched datum compiles to `{value, itemStyle}` — the clicked item IS the ECharts datum, not a `queryResult.rows` entry, so the binding resolves to nothing; on pivoting families (`seriesField`/stacked — `dataIndex` indexes the pivoted shape) it can resolve against the WRONG row. An animated chart's click carries `category`/`value`/`seriesName` but NO row. `table`/`kpi`/`stat`/`metric-strip`, by contrast, carry a ROW ONLY — never the `category`/`value`/`seriesName` triple a chart mark's click carries — so on those four `valueFrom`/`when.field` MUST name a real row field: a click-only token (`category`/`value`/`seriesName`), or an ABSENT `valueFrom` (which defaults to `category`), is never actionable and shows no affordance there. `kpi`/`stat`/`metric-strip` additionally bind from the panel's single result row only (`rows[0]`) — a field present on some other row but absent from `rows[0]` never satisfies a `when`/binding on those three either. A label template referencing a token this surface can't carry — a click-only token (`category`/`value`/`seriesName`) on `table`/`kpi`/`stat`/`metric-strip` — falls back to the literal, un-substituted label text rather than rendering the unresolvable token as empty, as does a row field that is present but null on the clicked row (a data-dependent case: rows differ).

ContextActionWhen.description: Optional visibility guard on a context-menu action (ADR-0035): the action is shown only when the clicked datum has a non-null value for `field`. v1 supports field-presence only (e.g. show 'Open in CRM' only on rows that carry an account id).

field.description: Row field name that must be present and non-null on the clicked datum for this action to appear.

ActionBinding.description: One param bound by a context-menu action (DVT-2104). Lets a single drill/overlay/filter action bind a COMPOUND key — e.g. (region, quarter) — instead of one param. Mutually exclusive with the scalar `param`/`valueFrom`/`valueType` form on the same action.

param.description: Params key set on the target (which must declare a matching named placeholder %(param)s).

valueFrom.description: Which part of the click supplies this value: 'category' (default), 'value', 'seriesName', or a field name read from the clicked row. For tables, use a field name.

valueType.description: Type the clicked value is coerced to before binding. Default string.

FilterAction.description: Context-menu action (ADR-0035) that cross-filters the CURRENT page: sets `{ param: clickedValue }` into the page's filter store and re-queries every panel that declares the param key — the same value→query binding contract and targeting as a `filter` control / `drill` (ADR-0028 §1/§4), sourced from a right-click instead of a control. Drill WITHOUT navigating away.

label.description: Menu item text. May template the clicked datum, e.g. "Filter page to {category}".

icon.description: Optional named icon shown beside the label.

param.description: Params key set on this page's panels (which must declare a matching named placeholder %(param)s and a data.params entry). The clicked value overwrites that value only — never interpolated, never reorders (ADR-0028).

valueFrom.description: Which part of the click supplies the bound value: 'category' (default), 'value', 'seriesName', or a field name read from the clicked row. For tables, use a field name. Same vocabulary as Drill.valueFrom.

valueType.description: Type the clicked value is coerced to before binding (defense-in-depth; binding is the security boundary). Default string.

bindings.description: Bind several params from one click (DVT-2104). Mutually exclusive with the scalar `param`. Prefer this for compound keys.

targets.description: Which panels re-query. "all" (default) = every panel on the page that declares the param key; or an explicit list of panel ids. A panel that doesn't declare the param key is never re-fetched regardless. Same semantics as FilterSpec.targets.

DrillAction.description: Context-menu action (ADR-0035) that navigates to a target page with the clicked value bound in — identical to the `drill` object (ADR-0028), but as a right-click menu item. This is the ONLY supported drill trigger (DVT-555): the bare `drill` property is retained for back-compat but is inert; all drill navigation must be wired via this action. One source can offer several drill destinations by adding multiple drill actions.

label.description: Menu item text. May template the clicked datum, e.g. "Open {category} detail".

icon.description: Optional named icon shown beside the label.

param.description: Params key set on the target page's panels (which must declare a matching named placeholder %(param)s).

valueFrom.description: Which part of the click supplies the bound value: 'category' (default), 'value', 'seriesName', or a field name read from the clicked row. For tables, use a field name.

valueType.description: Type the clicked value is coerced to before binding. Default string.

bindings.description: Bind several params from one click (DVT-2104). Mutually exclusive with the scalar `param`. Prefer this for compound keys.

LinkAction.description: Context-menu action (ADR-0035) that opens a URL templated with the clicked datum's values — the 'navigate to a related object' case (open a record in a CRM, ticket, or another tool). The URL's scheme is an authored literal (NOT templated) and must be https | mailto | tel; javascript:/data:/file:/vbscript:/scheme-relative are rejected. Every {token} value is encodeURIComponent-encoded before substitution, so a viewer-supplied value is data, never structure (ADR-0028 principle transposed to URLs). Carries no code.

label.description: Menu item text. May template the clicked datum, e.g. "Open {account} in CRM".

icon.description: Optional named icon shown beside the label.

url.description: URL template. Resolved scheme must be https | mailto | tel (the regex `pattern` here is a cheap first gate, NOT the security boundary — the boundary is a WHATWG URL parse run at render-time (web/src/linkSafety.ts); author-time enforcement is NOT implemented — tracked as DVT-2819; ADR-0035 §3). {token} placeholders ({category}/{value}/{seriesName}/{<field>}) interpolate the clicked datum, encodeURIComponent-encoded. A {token} may appear ONLY in the path/query/fragment — never in the scheme or authority (host/userinfo/port) position; a non-empty userinfo (user:pass@host) is rejected (host-spoofing guard). A missing token disables the action rather than producing a broken URL.

target.description: Where to open: 'tab' (default, new tab with rel=noopener noreferrer) or 'self' (same tab).

CopyAction.description: Context-menu action (ADR-0035) that copies part of the clicked datum to the clipboard. Client-only — no backend, no query.

icon.description: Optional named icon shown beside the label.

copy.description: What to copy: 'value' (default — the clicked value), 'row' (the whole row, tab-separated), or a field name (that field's value).

ExportAction.description: Context-menu action (ADR-0035) that exports data anchored on the clicked datum. scope 'row' exports the clicked row client-side over already-fetched data; scope 'result' exports the panel's full result via the server-enforced, audited export endpoint (DVT-137).

label.description: Menu item text, e.g. "Export this row (CSV)".

icon.description: Optional named icon shown beside the label.

scope.description: What to export: 'row' (default — the clicked row, client-side) or 'result' (the panel's full result via the audited DVT-137 export path).

OpenOverlayAction.description: Context-menu action (ADR-0036) that presents a target page as a modal/drawer overlay with the clicked value bound in — a superset of drill (it binds the same way) that does NOT navigate away. targetPage is usually a hidden page. Carries no code.

label.description: Menu item text. May template the clicked datum, e.g. "Open {category} detail".

icon.description: Optional named icon shown beside the label.

param.description: Params key set on the target page's panels (which must declare a matching named placeholder %(param)s).

valueFrom.description: Which part of the click supplies the bound value: 'category' (default), 'value', 'seriesName', or a field name read from the clicked row. For tables, use a field name.

valueType.description: Type the clicked value is coerced to before binding. Default string.

bindings.description: Bind several params from one click (DVT-2104). Mutually exclusive with the scalar `param`. Prefer this for compound keys.

present.description: How the target page is presented. modal = centered; drawer = slide-over. Default modal.

side.description: Drawer side (ignored for modal). Default right.

id.description: Stable panel ID. Must match layout items[*].i.

title.description: Panel header text. Supports {{ field | agg | format }} interpolation resolved against the panel's query result. Empty string ('') renders no header — common for text/html panels.

subtitle.description: Optional secondary line rendered beneath the panel title in muted text. Supports {{ field | agg | format }} interpolation resolved against the panel's query result. Omit to show no subtitle.

spec.description: Element spec. The valid shape is selected by `type`: chart:* → ChartSpec (ECharts passthrough), metric-strip → MetricStripSpec, kpi → KpiSpec, text → TextSpec, html → HtmlSpec, table → TableSpec, hero → HeroSpec, stat → StatSpec, media → MediaSpec, divider → DividerSpec, section → SectionPanelSpec, filter → FilterSpec.

overrides.description: Per-panel token overrides. Highest priority in resolution order. Bare (text/html) panels stay transparent unless they override panel.background here. SECURITY (ADR-0032 §2): an override value is read straight into an inline-style color / ECharts color sink, so the gate is default-deny — every override value is a ColorTokenValue (no url()/image-set() CSS-resource smuggling under the headless renderer, ADR-0024) UNLESS its key is a known non-color family (a dimensional/typographic suffix: .shadow/.size/.weight/.family/.radius/…), which stays loose TokenValue. This closes the whole class of color-override sinks (chart.series.N, *.color, *.background, text.*, color.*, accent.*, heatmap.*) rather than allow-listing them one at a time.

allOf.$comment: SETTLED (DVT-2720): the ground is the absence of a CLICKED datum — the renderer emits no per-datum click event carrying {category}/{value}/{seriesName} bindings for these nine types. That no-clicked-datum ground alone covers all nine and is primary. It is NOT the absence of data or query binding: text/html/hero CAN interpolate {{ field | agg | format }} against data rows (TextSpec.markdown, HtmlSpec.html, HeroSpec), and Panel.data is ungated on every panel type, chart or not — 'no datum' and 'no query binding' are the wrong reasons and must not creep back in. The hero-vs-stat split is not about panel shape either (both aggregate to a single value) — it is about which types resolve a query row into a clickable datum: DVT-2722 (non-chart parity) scopes kpi/stat/metric-strip/table cells because those DO resolve a row into a click target; these nine never do. A second, narrower ground applies to a subset: on filter/filter-bar/container, left-click already means 'operate this control / its children' — a second left-click meaning is a direct conflict; on html left-click already means 'follow the embedded anchor / authored content' — HtmlSpec.html is sanitized HTML and the sanitizer preserves anchors (DOMPurify's html USE_PROFILES keeps <a>, and HtmlPanel's config only adds target/rel — javascript: hrefs are neutralized by DOMPurify's built-in scheme allowlist, not by stripping the anchor, web/src/components/HtmlPanel.tsx:29-34,47), so an onClick there would collide with an already-clickable embedded link the same way it would on filter/container. divider/section are pure chrome. Recorded here deliberately because relaxing a schema restriction later is non-breaking, while adding one after authors depend on onClick on these types is breaking. This set is changed only through a ticket that first measures stored specs, since widening the exclusion later is a breaking change.

background.description: Per-page canvas background — any CSS background value (solid, gradient, image). Makes each page its own visual 'world'. Falls back to the page.background token. PRECEDENCE (DVT-2376): this field is the MOST SPECIFIC form of page background and WINS over a `page.background` key set in theme.page.theme.overrides — it is NOT a lower tier of the token cascade and is NOT overridden by the page theme tier. The surface reads `sanitizeBackground(page.background) ?? resolvedTokens['page.background']`; set one or the other, not both.

hidden.description: When true, this page is excluded from default page-tab navigation but remains fully authored, editable, and selectable in edit mode, and is a valid target for drill and openOverlay (ADR-0036). Defaults to false. PRESENTATION only, NOT access control — a hidden page's data is subject to the same RBAC as any page.

PageTheme.description: Per-page theme tier (DVT-2376, page-theming epic Lane 2). Inserts TWO tiers into the token cascade ABOVE the dashboard's own theme and BELOW panel/element overrides, so one dashboard can carry pages in different moods (a light overview page and a dark deep-dive page). Full cascade, lowest→highest: builtin defaults → org branding themeTokens → theme.preset → theme.tokens.primitive → .semantic → .component → theme.overrides → page.theme.preset → page.theme.overrides → panel.overrides. The page preset deliberately sits ABOVE dashboard theme.overrides: otherwise a dark page under a light dashboard override set would be impossible to express. Presets stay macros, never gates — every value a preset supplies is a plain token an author can override per key at this or any higher tier, and the overrides path never depends on any preset.

preset.description: Named theme preset applied to THIS PAGE ONLY (ADR-0043 preset semantics, page-scoped by DVT-2376). Ambient tier, exactly like theme.preset: it seeds token values but key presence here does NOT force over authored raw-ECharts detail (DVT-995 — only explicit tiers force). Off-list values are rejected at schema validation; fail-closed at resolve time (an unknown name seeds an empty tier, never a fallback preset).

overrides.description: Page-scoped explicit override tier (DVT-2376). Key presence = explicit intent: a key here FORCES field-wise over authored ECharts detail (series itemStyle.color, root color, textStyle.color/fontSize), the same way theme.overrides forces at dashboard scope and panel.overrides at panel scope — ambient tiers (any preset, theme.tokens.*) never do. Sits ABOVE theme.overrides and page.theme.preset, BELOW panel.overrides (a panel wins per key). Gated by ThemeTokenMap (DVT-294): colors are default-deny ColorTokenValue — url()/image-set() are rejected, the same SSRF/exfil sink the dashboard tier closes. NOTE: a CSS GRADIENT is NOT a legal color-token value at this or any other tier (ColorTokenValue admits {ref}/hex/rgb()/hsl()/named colors only) — author a page gradient with the page's own `background` field, which routes through the sanitizeBackground allowlist instead. NOTE: a `page.background` key here does NOT override that `background` field, which is the more specific explicit form and wins.

TabBar.description: Page-tab navigation control for a multi-page dashboard (pages[]). Declarative and fully configurable (DVT-174) — no callbacks. Rendered in the editor, the chrome-less /present viewer, and canvas full-bleed dashboards. Single-page dashboards render no tab chrome.

position.description: Where the tab control sits. top/bottom/left/right dock it to an edge; 'free' floats it at `placement` (used by full-bleed canvas dashboards where no edge gutter is reserved). Defaults to 'top'.

layout.description: How the tabs flow: 'horizontal' (a row), 'vertical' (a column), or 'stacked' (a row that wraps onto multiple lines on overflow). Defaults to 'horizontal'.

size.description: Tab-bar sizing (Lane-1 page rhythm). The enum keys map to fixed fontSize/padX/padY values — sm:{fontSize:12,padX:14,padY:8}, md:{fontSize:13,padX:20,padY:10}, lg:{fontSize:14,padX:24,padY:13} (TabBar.tsx's current size map) — the object form is the source of truth underneath (doctrine: every enum shorthand has a numeric sibling).

oneOf.description: Honored by the renderer since 1B (TabBar.tsx reads fontSize/padX/padY directly). The Dashboard-page editor's size control still only emits the enum form and disables itself against an object-form size, since it has no editor UI for custom numeric sizing yet.

placement.description: Float position for `position: 'free'` — a percentage offset (0–100) from the top-left of the viewport. Ignored for edge-docked positions. Defaults to top-left.

DvtRef.description: A named-function reference — the ADR-0014/0016 ECharts escape hatch in pure JSON. Where ECharts wants a callback or template a format object can't express, the spec carries {"$dvtRef": "<kind>:<name>@<version>"} and the renderer substitutes the registered implementation at compile time. The id MUST be versioned (the `@<version>` suffix is the determinism guarantee — a spec pinned to `@1` renders identically until it explicitly moves to `@2`) and MUST name a registered id: the enumerable set is the canonical manifest spec/schema/dvtref-registry.json. The hard write-time check is the Go validator pass ValidateDvtRefs (it fires on every $dvtRef anywhere in the spec, including inside ChartSpec passthrough nodes the schema can't reach); this $def documents the same contract and constrains the id wherever it is referenced by name.

$dvtRef.description: Versioned $dvtRef id, format <kind>:<name>@<version>. Must be one of the registered ids (spec/schema/dvtref-registry.json). An unknown or unsupported-version id is rejected at write time.
